<objective>
Build the D-14 token namespace boundary and SC4's automated proof: `app/tokens/venue.css` as a
venue-themable contract with hex-only fallbacks, `lib/theme/venue-tokens.ts` as a total resolver that
structurally cannot return a failing set, and two tripwire tests — an 18-pair contrast sweep and a
namespace-boundary scan.

Purpose: SC4 says "no venue theme value can produce a text/background pair below WCAG AA 4.5:1 — proven
by an automated guardrail test". D-14 keeps SC4 whole in 01.1: build the boundary **and** the guardrail
now, seeded with Cena's own pairing as the single member of the curated set. Retrofitting a namespace
later means re-cutting every token consumer; doing it now costs almost nothing. And the sweep is not
vacuous with one member — it is a regression guard on Cena's own AA compliance, which the design
project's contrast card currently proves only by hand.

Output: the venue namespace, the resolver, the sweep, and the boundary scan.

**Enabling relationship:** this plan delivers no requirement ID. It is the hard prerequisite for
THEME-01..04, which belong to a **later milestone** and are explicitly not claimed here. Under the
revised D-02, v1 ships exactly one brand — Cena's — on every surface, so **nothing in v1 consumes the
venue half of this boundary.** Building it anyway is D-14's decision, taken deliberately.

**Two verified defects in the research reference implementation are the reason the oracle pins exist.**
Both fail *open* — they report contrast that does not exist. `01.1-UI-SPEC.md` § "Contrast Guardrail
Contract" records them and their symptoms; plan 01.1-02 already implemented `contrastRatio` correctly
and pinned it. This plan re-asserts the same four pins inside the sweep file, deliberately and
redundantly, because `01.1-UI-SPEC.md` mandates the sweep assert them before it asserts anything about
the palette.
</objective>

  <name>Task 1: Author the venue token namespace and the total resolver</name>
  <files>app/tokens/venue.css, app/globals.css, lib/theme/venue-tokens.ts</files>
  <read_first>
    - `app/tokens/cena.css` and `app/tokens/primitives.css` as written by plan 01.1-05 — the shape to mirror, and the exact `--cena-*` names the fallbacks map onto
    - `app/globals.css` lines 1-6 as edited by plan 01.1-05 — the import block the third token import joins
    - `app/globals.css` `@theme inline` block — the `inline` idiom the repo already uses (`--font-sans: var(--font-sans)`), so this is a continuation, not a new concept
    - `.planning/phases/01.1-design-system-migration/01.1-UI-SPEC.md` § "Token Namespace Contract" — the three-layer table and all six rules
    - `.planning/phases/01.1-design-system-migration/01.1-RESEARCH.md` § "Pattern 2 — The Cena/venue token contract in Tailwind v4" — the 45-token extraction from the diner template and the four findings, especially the raw-ramp leak
    - `lib/theme/contrast.ts` (plan 01.1-02) — the `contrastRatio` signature the resolver consumes
    - `lib/venue-routes.ts` — the pure-module convention
  </read_first>
  <reversibility rating="reversible">The namespace is a naming convention, not a data migration, and the guardrail is purely additive. If the theming milestone later wants a different token vocabulary, changing it means renaming custom properties that nothing in v1 reads.</reversibility>
  <action>
    Three files, one commit.

    **`app/tokens/venue.css` (new).** Declare the venue-themable contract. Nine tokens, matching the
    semantic surface the diner template actually consumes: `--venue-ink`, `--venue-paper`,
    `--venue-surface`, `--venue-accent`, `--venue-accent-ink`, `--venue-muted-ink`, `--venue-rule`, plus
    the two family slots `--font-venue-display` and `--font-venue-body`. That set is small on purpose —
    PROJECT.md excludes deep per-venue customisation because restaurants would make ugly menus and visual
    quality is the differentiator.

    Two structural rules govern this file and both are mechanical, not stylistic. **(a)** Every colour
    token is declared inside an `@theme inline` block. Without `inline`, Tailwind emits `var(--color-x)`
    where `--color-x: var(--venue-ink)` resolves in `:root`'s scope, so a nested override on the menu root
    is ignored — Tailwind documents this as the exact scope-resolution failure `inline` exists to fix.
    Copy the `@theme inline` shape from `app/globals.css`; do not author a non-inline `@theme` block.
    **(b)** Every fallback value is a literal six-digit sRGB hex. Hex is what a colour picker produces, it
    is what WCAG 2.1's relative-luminance formula is defined over, and it removes any colour-space
    conversion dependency from inside a legal release gate.

    Seed the fallbacks with Cena's own values, written as literal hex rather than as `var(--cena-*)`
    references — a reference would import a Cena ramp identifier into this file, which rule 3 of the Token
    Namespace Contract forbids and `tests/theme/token-boundary.test.ts` will fail on. Use
    `--venue-paper: #FFFFFF`, `--venue-ink: #1C2625`, `--venue-muted-ink: #526260`,
    `--venue-surface: #EDF2F1`, `--venue-accent: #0B5FA5`, `--venue-accent-ink: #FFFFFF`,
    `--venue-rule: #DCE4E3`.

    Write the file header as the contract itself: state that no Cena ramp identifier may appear here, that
    values are hex only, that status colours (warning, danger, success) are Cena-fixed on every surface
    forever and therefore deliberately absent from this namespace, and that **nothing in v1 consumes these
    tokens** — under the revised D-02, v1 renders every surface including the diner menu in Cena's own
    design, and these are a contract for a later milestone. Cite `01.1-UI-SPEC.md` § Token Namespace
    Contract.

    Record the **D-03 constraint** on the two font slots in the same header, because it is a mechanical
    limit rather than a preference: `next/font` resolves family names at build time, so a dynamic family
    name cannot work, and a venue's typeface choice must therefore be a **closed, curated set of 3 to 4
    statically-declared instances selected by class name** — never a free font picker. Each pairing must be
    self-hosted and verified for the RO and HU diacritics before it ships, because a picker would put
    third-party bytes on the diner critical path and regress SC1. Seed the two slots with Cena's own
    pairing, which is the single member of that set in v1 (D-09).

    Add no media query keyed on the operating system's colour preference anywhere in this file. Under
    D-10 the diner menu never follows the device's dark preference, and auto-darkening would invalidate
    every ratio the sweep measures.

    **`app/globals.css` (modify).** Add `@import "./tokens/venue.css";` to the existing leading import
    block, after the two imports plan 01.1-05 added. Change nothing else — in particular leave the spacing
    scale and both width-shield blocks byte-identical, because `tests/lib/theme-width-scale.test.ts` reads
    this file and pins two of those values literally.

    **`lib/theme/venue-tokens.ts` (new).** Export three things.

    `VenueTokens` — the resolved token record, one key per `--venue-*` colour token, each typed as a
    six-digit hex string.

    `CONTRAST_PAIRS` — an explicit adjacency list of the 18 pairs `01.1-UI-SPEC.md` § "The sweep" measured,
    each entry carrying a foreground token name, a background token name, a numeric threshold, and a
    `rendersAt` description used in failure messages. Thresholds are **not uniform**: rows 1 to 13 and row
    18 carry 4.5, rows 15 to 17 carry **3.0** (the WCAG 1.4.11 non-text threshold — input, checkbox and
    idle-chip boundaries; the focus ring and selected-state border; the banner rule), and row 14 — the
    decorative divider — is marked **exempt** and carries no threshold, because WCAG 1.4.11 exempts pure
    decoration. Applying 4.5 uniformly produces false failures and is precisely how a guardrail gets
    weakened until it passes.

    Include the two status rows permanently, not as v1-only checks: `warning-ink` on `warning-soft` (the
    DINE-04 last-good banner, a release gate) and `danger` on both `paper` and `danger-soft` (the
    INGEST-06 unverified-AI-field marker, a release gate). Status colours stay Cena-fixed even when venue
    theming ships, but because they will eventually sit on venue-controlled paper, their pairs stay in the
    sweep forever.

    `resolveVenueTheme(input)` — a **total** function returning a discriminated union: either a success
    carrying a complete `VenueTokens`, or a failure carrying the list of pairs that fell below threshold.
    It takes the few inputs a venue actually supplies (brand colour, paper/ink polarity, pairing id) and
    **derives** every text token by picking, from a fixed ink/paper candidate pair, whichever reaches the
    higher ratio against each surface. It must never return a silently-bad set. This shape is what makes
    the guardrail a property of the type rather than of a validation step a caller can forget — which is
    why it is authored now, in 01.1, even though Phase 4's owner UI is its first caller.

    Record in the module header that THEME-04 enforcement belongs on the **write path** (Server Action plus
    Zod), not client-only: a direct PostgREST or RPC caller bypasses the UI entirely, and this mirrors the
    existing `createVenueSchema` ↔ CHECK-constraint doctrine already established in the repo. Record also
    that venue theme values must reach CSS via a `style` prop on the diner page's root Server Component,
    baked at prerender — never a `<style dangerouslySetInnerHTML>` (a string-interpolation injection
    surface), never middleware or `proxy.ts` (forces the route dynamic), never a client fetch (forbidden
    by CLAUDE.md, and causes FOUC on the DINE-03 critical path).
  </action>
  <verify>

    - `pnpm exec vitest run tests/lib/theme-width-scale.test.ts` exits 0 — the spacing scale and shields were not disturbed
    - `lib/theme/venue-tokens.ts` exports `CONTRAST_PAIRS` and `resolveVenueTheme`, and `CONTRAST_PAIRS` has at least 18 entries
    - `lib/theme/venue-tokens.ts` contains at least one entry whose threshold is `3` and at least one marked exempt — the thresholds are not uniform

  <action>
    Write this test to fail first — run it before `CONTRAST_PAIRS` is complete and confirm it is red —
    then complete the table.

    Create `tests/theme/venue-contrast-guardrail.test.ts` (node environment). Open with a header block, in
    the style of `tests/lib/theme-width-scale.test.ts`, recording the two defects in the research reference
    implementation this file exists to catch: the un-linearised blue channel, which inflates every ratio
    involving blue — including every pair against the azure accent — and returns 387.78 instead of 21 for
    black on white; and the shorthand-hex coercion, which silently returns 2.51 for a three-digit input.
    Both fail **open**: they report contrast that does not exist, on a gate PROJECT.md makes legally

    **Block 1 — oracle pins, asserted before anything else.** Assert `contrastRatio('#000000', '#FFFFFF')`
    is 21.00 to two decimals; `contrastRatio('#767676', '#FFFFFF')` is 4.542 within ±0.005 (the canonical
    AA near-pass); `contrastRatio('#777777', '#FFFFFF')` is 4.478 within ±0.005 (the canonical AA
    near-fail); and that a three-digit input throws rather than coercing. This duplicates
    `tests/theme/contrast-oracle.test.ts` deliberately — `01.1-UI-SPEC.md` mandates that this file assert

    Create `tests/theme/token-boundary.test.ts` (node environment). Open with a header block naming the two
    defect classes it guards: a Cena ramp identifier leaking into a namespace a venue is supposed to be
    able to re-map (a raw ramp name can never be re-mapped by a theme, which is the structural failure the

    writing a second extractor — that function is the repo's established read-a-stylesheet-as-data idiom
    and `01.1-PATTERNS.md` names it as the one to copy.

    Assert four things.

    1. **No Cena ramp identifier in the venue namespace.** Scan `app/tokens/venue.css` for each of the four
       ramp prefixes and assert zero matches, with a failure message naming which prefix was found and
       stating that a raw ramp name can never be re-mapped by a theme.

    2. **Hex only.** Extract every `--venue-*` declaration and assert each colour value matches strict
       six-digit `#rrggbb`. Reject three-digit shorthand explicitly — the contrast function throws on it,
       so a shorthand value here would take down the sweep at Phase 4 rather than now. Guard non-vacuity by
       asserting the extracted map has at least 7 entries first.

       media query keyed on the device's colour scheme. This satisfies D-10 at the strongest available
       level: rather than asserting that no such selector *touches* a venue token, assert none exists at
       all, which is both simpler and stricter.

    4. **The dark mechanism survives.** Assert `app/globals.css` still declares the dark variant as a
       class-based custom variant. D-10 keeps the mechanism while wiring no dark UI; a test that only
       forbade the media query could pass on a file that had lost dark support entirely.

    Note in the header that under the revised D-02 the raw-ramp normalisation is no longer a *brand* breach
    — v1 ships one brand — but remains a *structural* requirement, because a raw ramp name is un-themable
    by construction.
  </action>

<threat_model>
**Review level: OWASP ASVS L1.** This is the level appropriate to a phase that changes no auth logic, no authorization boundary and no data path — 01.1 is a visual and vocabulary migration, and every plan that touches a security-relevant file holds it byte-identical under a `git diff` gate rather than reviewing it. **Block on: `high`.** Every threat rated `high` or `critical` carries a `mitigate` disposition with a named, gated implementation; `medium` and `low` may carry `accept` with a stated rationale.

## Trust Boundaries

| Boundary | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| venue owner → CSS custom property | In Phase 4 an owner-supplied colour becomes a CSS value in prerendered HTML. This is the single new attack surface 01.1 creates. |
| direct PostgREST / RPC caller → venue theme row | A caller that bypasses the owner UI entirely must still be unable to store a sub-AA theme. |
| stylesheet → contrast sweep | The sweep reads token values out of `app/tokens/cena.css`, so a token edit is measured rather than assumed. |

## STRIDE Threat Register

| Threat ID | Category | Component | Severity | Disposition | Mitigation Plan |
|-----------|----------|-----------|----------|-------------|-----------------|
| T-01.1-01 | Tampering | CSS injection via a venue theme value | high | mitigate | Constrain the venue namespace to strict `#rrggbb` at the Zod boundary and assert it in `tests/theme/token-boundary.test.ts`. Inject via React's `style` prop (attribute-escaped) on the diner page's root Server Component — never `<style dangerouslySetInnerHTML>`, never middleware, never a client fetch. Recorded in the `lib/theme/venue-tokens.ts` header so Phase 4 inherits the rule. |
| T-01.1-02 | Repudiation | Accessibility bypass on a legal gate | high | mitigate | THEME-04 is enforced on the **write path** (Server Action plus Zod `superRefine`), not client-only, because a direct PostgREST or RPC caller bypasses the UI. `resolveVenueTheme` is total and cannot return a silently-bad set, so the guarantee is a property of the type rather than of a call someone can forget. The 18-pair sweep is the test-time proof. |
| T-01.1-26 | Tampering | A threshold weakened to make the sweep pass | high | mitigate | Thresholds are non-uniform by contract (4.5 for text, 3.0 for WCAG 1.4.11 non-text, one explicit decorative exemption) and are asserted from `CONTRAST_PAIRS` rather than inlined. A fetched ramp value that fails is reverted to the locked value; the guardrail is the arbiter, not the imported document. |
| T-01.1-27 | Repudiation | The sweep silently emptying | medium | mitigate | `CONTRAST_PAIRS.length >= 8` and a minimum-16-entry guard on the palette extraction, both asserted before the sweep runs. Each of the three tests in this plan is observed failing before it is accepted. |
| T-01.1-28 | Tampering | Status colour themed until a warning becomes invisible | high | mitigate | Warning, danger and success are Cena-fixed on every surface permanently and are deliberately absent from the `--venue-*` namespace. Because they will eventually sit on venue-controlled paper, their pairs are permanent sweep rows, not v1-only checks. |
</threat_model>
